findings.title: NPE when the all-clients resource does not exist
findings.body: In `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, when the per-client resource is absent, the code calls `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`. That method returns null in several situations (e.g. when the resource type is unknown, when schema support is not active, or simply when the corresponding "Clients" resource row has not been created yet in the DB). The very next line passes that potentially-null resource to `authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource)`, which will throw a NullPointerException. The method must null-check the result before using it (and should not silently return false when the all-clients resource is missing - that is a real production scenario for any realm that enabled ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 before this PR was deployed, because the new resource type is added to the schema but never instantiated in the DB).

findings.title: No migration to create the new "Clients" resource type resource for existing realms
findings.body: `init(...)` early-returns whenever `realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null`, so it only runs the first time admin permissions are enabled on a realm. This PR adds a new resource type (`Clients`) to `SCHEMA` and to `init`, but it provides no upgrade path for realms that already enabled V2 admin permissions prior to this change: their authorization database will only contain the "Users" resource type resource (and scopes registered at the time), and the new "Clients" resource type resource will never be created. After upgrade, `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, "Clients")` returns null, causing the NPE described above in `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission`. A migration step (or at least a defensive null guard in the consumer) is required before this PR can be safely released to existing V2 users.

findings.title: canMapRoles / canMapCompositeRoles / canMapClientScopeRoles ignore the MANAGE_CLIENTS realm role
findings.body: `canManage(ClientModel)`, `canConfigure(ClientModel)`, `canManageClientScopes()` and `canView()` all explicitly fall back to the realm-level `MANAGE_CLIENTS` (and/or `VIEW_CLIENTS`) admin role via `root.hasOneAdminRole(...)` before consulting the FGAP scopes. `canMapRoles`, `canMapCompositeRoles` and `canMapClientScopeRoles` skip that fallback entirely and only call `hasPermission(client, ...)`. A realm administrator who has been granted the classic `MANAGE_CLIENTS` realm role (and not the equivalent FGAP scope) will pass `canManage(client)` but fail `canMapRoles(client)`, so they cannot add client roles/composites - which is a behavior break versus V1 and an inconsistent permission model across the evaluator. The methods should check `MANAGE_CLIENTS` first, matching the pattern used elsewhere in this class.

findings.title: canView() ignores the FGAP MANAGE scope
findings.body: `canView()` is implemented as `canViewClientDefault() || hasPermission(VIEW)`. `canView(ClientScopeModel)` on the other hand returns true for either VIEW or MANAGE, and `canView(ClientModel)` returns true whenever `canConfigure(client)` (which ultimately honors FGAP MANAGE) returns true. The asymmetry means an admin that was granted only the `manage` scope for all clients (a perfectly normal FGAP grant) can configure a specific client and view it via `canView(ClientModel)` / `canView(ClientScopeModel)`, but `canView()` and `canList()` - which the listing endpoints rely on - return false, so the admin cannot browse the clients list. The scope check for `canView()` should also accept `MANAGE` (and `canManageClientScopes()` should likewise accept VIEW), mirroring the way the per-resource variants behave.

findings.title: Dead code in ClientPermissionsV2
findings.body: The class contains several pieces of unused code that should be removed before merge: the `private static final Logger logger` (line 51) is never referenced, the helper `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken)` (line 262) has no callers in this file or the codebase, and the imports that exist solely to support that helper (`ClientModelIdentity`, `DefaultEvaluationContext`, `EvaluationContext`, `AccessToken`, `Scope`, plus `TOKEN_EXCHANGE` and `Arrays`) are dead as a consequence. Either wire `getEvaluationContext` into `hasPermission` so policies can match on `kc.client.id`, or delete it together with its imports.

findings.title: Lazy initialization of clientPermissions is not thread-safe
findings.body: `clients()` does a non-synchronized check-then-set on the `clientPermissions` field. If two threads invoke `mgmt.clients()` concurrently, both can observe `clientPermissions == null` and each builds its own `ClientPermissionsV2`, leaving one instance to be silently discarded. The same pattern is already present for `userPermissions`, but adding a second unsynchronized lazy cache makes the problem more likely to be hit. Make the field `volatile` and/or guard the assignment (`synchronized`, `AtomicReference`, or eager init in the constructors).
